messages.subject: rouble o
parts:
Hi! 

I am working with 3D geometric morphometrics on dolphin vertebrae, I am working with four different but closely related species from the Southern Hemipshere. Among other things I am studying ontogeny patterns in vertebral shape. I am not quite interested in shape changes per se but in the direction of shape changes in an attempt to evidence evolutionary patterns in shape changes.

 

I was planning on using MorphoJ for most of the analyses but I was advised to use Geomorph for the trajectory analyses, since I was told by more experienced researchers that the “veccompare function” in MorphoJ is not the best approach for my data.

 

I haven't even get to run the trajectory.analysis because I am having trouble performing the gpa on my data. I am not a fluent R user, so I am having trouble loading my data in order to run the analysis. I tried loading a .csv file with all the landmark coordinates in the same row for each specimen but when I run the gpa I get an error:

> Y.gpa <- gpagen(X01Cvcoord)

Error in gpagen(X01Cvcoord) : Coordinates must be a 3D array

 

When I try to arrange my data with the function arrayaspecs I also get an error:

> arrayspecs(X01Cvcoord, 33, 3,byLand=FALSE) 

Error in arrayspecs(X01Cvcoord, 33, 3, byLand = FALSE) : 

  unused argument (byLand = FALSE)

 

I am sure that I am doing something wrong when loading or organizing the data, but I cannot find my error! I know this is a silly question but I am stuck and my frustration is getting bigger by the minute!

Can anyone help me organizing my data to be loaded into R, please????

Thank you in advance!

messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] rouble o
parts:
Maria,

 

The error you are receiving with ‘arrayspecs’ is because you have included an argument that no longer exists. Current versions of the function do not require ‘byLand = …’.  If you remove that and try again things should work.

 

As you are new to R, I might suggest that you first examine the help files for particular functions prior to using them.  For example typing ‘?arrayspecs’ will display its help file.

 

Best,

 

Dean

parts:
Maria,

 

No, the number of landmarks is not going to be the number of points in the trajectory. The number of points refers to the ‘levels’ that comprise the trajectory, which are defined by the data you have and the hypothesis you are investigating (e.g., time points, environments, etc.).

 

To understand this, please refer to the help file for trajectory analysis. Additionally, a careful reading of the original literature where trajectory analysis was proposed would be useful.

Dean

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] rouble o
parts:
Maria,

The help page on this function has explicit details about the two options you have available:

1. YT ~ group, where Y are data and T means trajectory points, so if you have coordinates, then you need to concatenate coordinates T times for the t repeated points in the trajectories.
2. Y ~ group * T, where Y are data and the repeated points are found as additional rows in your Y matrix.

If p is the number of shape variables and t is the number of trajectory points, YT is an n x (pt) matrix.  Y is an (nt) x p matrix.

You are confusing the two.  You are putting in data for the second approach but have a design (right side of the equation) like the first approach.

The help page goes into more detail.

Mike
